points.description: Defines DHCP as a network management protocol for IP networks in which a DHCP server dynamically assigns an IP address and other network configuration parameters to devices. Equivalent wording is accepted. Mentioning RARP/BOOTP is not required.

States a use of DHCP: automatic configuration of end systems, which simplifies installation and configuration. Any one of the listed uses earns the mark: automatic (or manual) IP address assignment, or supplying extra configuration such as DNS server, netmask or default router. Equivalent wording is accepted.

rubric.notes: The question asks two things, so the 1 mark splits evenly: 0.5 for a correct definition (a protocol where a server dynamically assigns IP addresses and configuration to devices) and 0.5 for a correct use (automatic configuration, address assignment, or extra configuration parameters). The remark that DHCP replaced RARP and BOOTP is secondary detail and carries no separate point. Answers that give only a vague description, such as "it gives devices network settings", should be judged against the definition point.
